clue.text: Strike legislation rejected — left work

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word for legislation is read backwards

parts.note: a law is a piece of legislation
OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A union strikes after new laws are thrown out and members walk off the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' looks like the industrial action of the surface but is the definition, a hard blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy blow is called a wallop, so to strike hard is to wallop.

clue.text: A moral tale about female being friendly

indicators.note: the moral tale goes about, i.e. around, the female abbreviation

parts.note: a fable is a story with a moral

explanation.surface: A story with a lesson about a woman who is kind.
explanation.definitionFit: An affable person is good-natured and easy to talk to, i.e. friendly.

clue.text: Language progress comes after cutting connection short

indicators.note: the progress word is placed after the trimmed piece
cutting a word short removes its tail
short means the last letter of the connection word is dropped

parts.note: a link is a connection
go means proceed or make progress

explanation.surface: Talks progress only once the phone line is cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting ... short' drops the K from LINK, leaving LIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is informal for a language or jargon.

clue.text: Debts regularly seen to support scheme with regard to energy growth

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath, so the debts letters come below the scheme

parts.note: a plan is a scheme

indicators.note: every other letter of debts is taken, the second and fourth

parts.note: re means concerning, with regard to
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A financial plan propping up a green-energy growth scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes ET from Debts.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall broad-leaved tree common in city streets is a growth in the sense of something grown.

clue.text: Pudding that can come before order?

definitions.text: Pudding that can come before order?

parts.words: Pudding that can come before order?
parts.note: a classic baked fruit dessert whose name also precedes 'order' in the idiom for perfect neatness

explanation.surface: A riddle about which dessert might be served before the orders are taken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Apple-pie order' is an idiom meaning perfectly tidy, so the pudding's name can sit before the word 'order'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit dessert in pastry is a classic British pudding, and its name forms the idiom for neatness.

clue.text: Realise that is five in pain

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the pain word

parts.note: an ache is a pain
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A sufferer realises that a fifth bout of pain has arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise an ambition is to accomplish or attain it.

clue.text: Chaplain's flat rate, having no heart

definitions.note: the clue word with 's reads as 'chaplain is', so the definition is chaplain

parts.note: a pad is slang for a flat or home

indicators.note: the two middle letters of rate are removed

explanation.surface: A clergyman's apartment rent seems heartless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having no heart' removes AT from RATE, leaving RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is the services' name for a military chaplain or priest.

clue.text: Former soldiers caught on wrong side driven out!

parts.note: ex means former
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the letters of side are put wrong, into a new order

explanation.surface: Veterans caught on the wrong side of a line and expelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' turns SIDE into ISED.
explanation.definitionFit: An evil spirit that has been exorcised has been expelled, or driven out.

clue.text: Suggestion of popular ruler protecting pound

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: the ruler word wraps round and shields the pound letter

parts.note: a king is a ruler
L, from Latin libra, stands for a pound

explanation.surface: A hint that a well-liked monarch is guarding the currency.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkling is a slight hint or suggestion of something.

clue.text: End in French harbour after granny ate fish

indicators.note: the harbour word is placed after the granny and ate pieces

parts.note: the French word for end is fin
nan is a familiar word for a grandmother
had, as in 'had lunch', means ate
a dock is a harbour for ships

explanation.surface: A seaside scene: a French harbour where granny finishes off a fish supper.
explanation.walkthrough: FIN is French for 'end' (as at the close of a film).
explanation.definitionFit: This is a smoked haddock from Findon in Scotland, a kind of fish.

clue.text: Dated and wrong to be going round alone

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go round the word for alone, enclosing it
the letters of 'to be' are put wrong, i.e. into a new order

parts.note: sole means single or alone

explanation.surface: A warning that it is outdated and mistaken to go about by yourself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' turns TO BE into OBTE, and 'going round' places that around SOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of date and no longer in use is obsolete, i.e. dated.

clue.text: University College may be accepted by reformed idle mathematician

indicators.note: the college abbreviation is accepted into, i.e. put inside, the rearranged letters
reformed means formed again, so the letters of idle are rearranged

parts.note: UC is the usual abbreviation for University College

explanation.surface: A lazy scholar, once reformed, might get into University College.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be accepted by' is a containment signal: the college sits inside the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek author of the Elements is the most famous geometer, a mathematician.

clue.text: Case of dill imported by fruit vendor

indicators.note: the picked letters are brought into the fruit word

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

indicators.note: a case is the outside, so the first and last letters of dill are taken

explanation.surface: A greengrocer imports a crate of dill along with his fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case of' gives DL, the outside letters of dill.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedlar travels about selling small goods, so is a vendor.

clue.text: Throws company function, finding a dish from the north

parts.note: to lob is to throw in a high arc
a use is a function or purpose

explanation.surface: Someone hurls things at the firm's party and discovers northern food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'function' suggests a party but means use; lobscouse is a meat stew linked with Liverpool, origin of 'Scouse'.
explanation.definitionFit: This sailors' stew is associated with Liverpool in north-west England, a regional dish.

clue.text: Imagine vines developing with time

indicators.note: developing letters change shape, so vines are rearranged

parts.note: an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A wine grower pictures the vines maturing over the years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' turns VINES into ENVIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To envisage is to picture something in the mind, a synonym of imagine.

clue.text: Finished without love, albeit strangely true

indicators.note: the love letter is taken away

parts.note: over means finished
O, zero, is love in tennis

indicators.note: the letters of albeit are arranged strangely, into a new order

explanation.surface: A love affair has ended, yet oddly the feeling was genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' turns ALBEIT into ITABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Veritable means real or genuine, i.e. true.

clue.text: Marine ray will eat river fish

parts.note: marine means of the sea

indicators.note: the ray word swallows the river abbreviation

parts.note: a beam is a ray of light

explanation.surface: A sea ray feeding on a freshwater fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ray' looks like the fish but is a beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: The bream found in the sea is a common edible fish.

clue.text: Student trapped by crude chance

indicators.note: the student letter is caught inside the crude word

parts.note: earthy means coarse or crude
L is a learner, i.e. student, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A learner snared by a vulgar opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chance' is a noun here, as in 'not an earthly' meaning no chance at all.
explanation.definitionFit: In the British idiom 'not an earthly', the word stands for a chance of success.

clue.text: Horse around what in Spain is a tent

indicators.note: the horse word goes around the Spanish word

parts.note: a mare is a female horse
que is the Spanish for what

explanation.surface: A horse is led around a Spanish showground marquee.
explanation.definitionFit: A marquee is a large tent used for parties or shows.

clue.text: Doll oddly found in fairground attraction is an enigma

indicators.note: the picked letters are found inside the fairground word

parts.note: a ride is an attraction at a fair

indicators.note: the odd letters, first and third, of doll are taken

explanation.surface: A doll discovered on a fairground ride is a puzzling mystery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes DL from Doll.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a puzzle or mystery, as is an enigma.

clue.text: Affair giving rise to trouble with one lad

indicators.note: rise in a down clue means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
I is the Roman numeral for one
a son is a lad

explanation.surface: An affair that causes trouble involving a young man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving rise to' turns AIL upward into LIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a secret romantic relationship, an affair.

clue.text: Works out and breaks down

definitions.meaning: to work out a code or problem is to solve it
to break down under pressure is to give way

explanation.surface: Someone exercises and then collapses under the strain.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both solving a puzzle and collapsing under strain, two senses of one word.

clue.text: Rumour of cut being steep

indicators.note: a rumour is something heard, so the word for cut is said out loud

parts.note: to shear is to cut

explanation.surface: Gossip of a cut-throat move being sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheer cliff is very steep, almost vertical.

clue.text: Share a line, being sensible

parts.note: a ration is a fixed share

explanation.surface: Splitting a queue's place is the sensible thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Being rational means reasoning soundly, i.e. being sensible.

clue.text: Depressing experiences uncovered for title-holder

indicators.note: uncovered means the outer letters of the word are stripped

parts.note: downers are depressing experiences

explanation.surface: Gloomy times exposed for the holder of a championship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'title-holder' suggests a sports champion but means someone holding the legal title to property.
explanation.definitionFit: One who holds legal title to property is its proprietor.

clue.text: Saves on accommodation for domestic workers

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the saving word follows the accommodation

parts.note: a house is accommodation
to husband resources is to save them carefully

explanation.surface: A tip about cutting costs on rent and lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saves' looks like a noun but is the verb husbands, meaning to conserve.
explanation.definitionFit: Men who stay at home doing the housework while their partners earn are home-based workers.

clue.text: Fancy times with last of people in Cheddar perhaps!

parts.note: by means times, as in two by four

indicators.note: the picked letter goes inside the Cheddar word

parts.note: Cheddar Gorge is a famous gorge in Somerset, England

indicators.note: the final letter of people is taken

explanation.surface: An exclamation at seeing a fancy cheese on a platter with the last guests.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheddar is not cheese here: Cheddar Gorge is a limestone canyon in Somerset, England.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Fancy!' and 'By George!' are both old-fashioned exclamations of surprise.

clue.text: Border ran directly across mission

indicators.note: the letters run across the words, spanning their boundaries

explanation.surface: Someone crosses a border on a direct mission.
explanation.definitionFit: A task one is sent to perform is a mission, also called an errand.
